text:
incidents-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Titania dedicated pool reporting sustained GPU saturation (100% on all cards). Paging eng-oncall, eng-runtime, eng-sre. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/titania/pool/overview

oncall-ryan: I'm on it. Acknowledged. ETA 2m.

sre-jess: seeing sustained queue depth on Titania-prod, model `titania-gpt-large` spiking. autoscaler logs show 'scale_action_skipped: tenant_limit_reached'.

sre-jess: metrics snapshot:
```
gpu_util: 99-100%
queue_len: 620 -> 1100
avg_p50_latency: 220ms
p95_latency: 1.9s
autoscaler.reason: tenant_capacity_maxed
```

eng-runtime-leo: looks like tenant has pinned all dedicated GPUs and autoscaler can't allocate more because pool max_replicas_per_pool hit. Two options: 1) allow emergency burst from shared spare capacity (requires ops approval), 2) evict low-priority background jobs for Titania to free on-host memory, or 3) contact Titania for immediate slowdown.

acct-mgr-kate: @oncall-ryan @sre-jess customer impact? Are their production requests failing or just slower? Need to notify Titania CSM if we take any action.

csd-omar: Titania support reported 503s from some webhooks and elevated error rates since ~06:12 UTC. They're seeing timeouts for inference calls. Customer is waiting on a statement.

infra-ops-sam: I can provision emergency GPUs from the burst pool (`burst-reserve`) for up to 4 cards. That requires a manual override `rbctl pool burst-override --pool titania-dedicated --gpus 3 --reason "emergency saturation"`. Need approval from product or oncall to run.

oncall-ryan: Product to weigh in @product-maya, we need a go/no-go for emergency burst. If yes, Sam run the command and watch for downstream effects. If no, we start tenant throttling.

product-maya: For customer-facing impact we should enable burst if it resolves errors quickly. Approving emergency burst + billable usage for this event. Proceed. :+1:

infra-ops-sam: running override now:
```bash
rbctl pool burst-override --pool titania-dedicated --gpus 3 --reason "emergency saturation" --approve-by product-maya
```

infra-ops-sam: output: `override accepted, allocating 3 gpus from burst-reserve, allocation id br-9876`. Spinning up nodes, warming runtime.

incidents-bot: UPDATE: emergency burst initiated (br-9876). Notifying routing: Titania requests temporarily routed to new burst instances.

eng-runtime-leo: KV-cache warmup in progress. Observability: model warm-start logs show new workers joined, accepting requests.

sre-jess: queue draining. queue_len down 1100 -> 150 in 4m. p95 latency down 1.9s -> 320ms. Error rate dropping.

acct-mgr-kate: drafting customer note: "We've identified a capacity saturation in your dedicated pool and applied an emergency burst to stabilize traffic; we're investigating root cause and will follow up with a post-incident report." Will send after confirmation.

oncall-ryan: good. CS to send initial message. Also create incident record and link to runbook.

csd-omar: sent message to Titania CSM and primary contact. They acknowledged and are monitoring. Thanks team.

sre-jess: follow-up actions: 1) postmortem to analyze why tenant limit was hit (workload spike, misconfiguration), 2) evaluate autoscaler thresholds and pool max_replicas_per_pool, 3) consider soft-limits/early-warning alerts for tenant queue > 400.

product-maya: agree on follow-ups. Also coordinate billing/impact review with finance.

infra-ops-sam: scheduling capacity resize for Titania pool tomorrow 09:00 UTC if they approve committed increase.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation successful, error rate back to baseline. Closing paging loop. Please add timeline and notes to incident page: https://incidents.redwood/7751234567

oncall-ryan: closing here. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
